lessons: Image models ignore 'not a biplane': show only the engine nose or cockpit for Lindbergh-era aircraft so wing count cannot go wrong.
Never use dental or medical photos as a stand-in for a different property of the same alloy; use them only on the medical line.
Check the photo label against what the picture shows (a 1902 car is not a 1925 death).
Reserve illustration budget: convert real period photos (e.g. the Haynes 1894 car) first, then spend illustrations only where no photo fits.
